title: Inspections tab links and buttons, phone use, and the inspection's asset
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in with 'Customers - View' and 'Work orders - View'.
  2. An asset with inspections; a phone (or narrow viewport); at least one pre-release inspection backfilled at migration; and an inspection whose work order's asset was later changed.
custom_steps:
1. Confirm everything that navigates is a link and everything that changes something is a button.
2. On a phone, confirm every column's information stays reachable and the page does not scroll sideways; the filter row wraps and keeps its counts.
3. Confirm the tab shows what was inspected (asset stored on the inspection at creation), not a view that follows a later work-order asset change; confirm a pre-release inspection was backfilled from its work order's asset.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Everything that navigates is a link and everything that changes something is a button.
  • The tab is usable on a phone: every column's information stays reachable and the page does not scroll sideways.
  • The filter row wraps on a phone rather than scrolling out of view, and keeps its counts.
  • An inspection records the asset it was run on, stored on the inspection at creation rather than derived through its work order, and pre-release inspections are backfilled from their work order's asset at migration.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-8181, story SV-9103 (S5 — Inspection history on the asset record); Digital Inspections V2 specification, Confluence page 768507905, section S5; read on 22 September 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S5-R14: “Everything that navigates will be a link and everything that changes something will be a button”
  • S5-R15: “The tab will be usable on a phone. Every column's information will remain reachable and the page will not scroll sideways”
  • S5-R16: “The filter row will wrap on a phone rather than scrolling out of view, and will keep its counts”
  • S5-R21: “An inspection records the asset it was run on, stored on the inspection when it is created rather than derived through its work order. A work order carries exactly one asset and that asset can be changed later, so this tab is a record of what was inspected rather than a view that follows a later correction. Inspections that exist before this release are backfilled from their work order’s asset at migration, without which this tab cannot show history”

Last checked against build v26.36.8-2a64085 on 10/1/2026.
